artifacts.summary: Recommends a narrowly-scoped state.json/.orchestrator-handoff.json demotion (completed -> partial) inside WORK (i) of orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh for exit codes {2,3,4,5} on an implement-phase dispatch, over the larger reorder-into-two-commits alternative; corrects task 304's monotonic-max reasoning and flags exit 6 as a non-failure per git-staging-scope.md's V9 semantics.

memory_candidates.content: In this codebase's orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, state.json's 'persisted_status' field in the final emitted JSON is read FRESH from state.json at the very end of the script (after every WORK block), decoupled from 'status' (the dispatch's self-report). Any future postflight correction/demotion of state.json requires no extra wiring to appear in the emitted JSON -- persisted_status already reflects it. The script's own header comment documents this divergence as intentional design, not a bug.

git-commit-scoped.sh exit code 6 (V9, out-of-repository pathspec drop) means the commit DID land successfully for every valid path -- per context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's own table, it is 'observability, not a refusal.' Any future logic that groups git-commit-scoped.sh's exit codes for a severity/trust decision (not just logging) must exclude 6 from a 'genuine failure' set, unlike codes 2/3/4 (no commit created) and 5 (commit created but a named intended path missing from HEAD).

The monotonic-max status clamp (scripts/lib/status-vocabulary.sh's status_vocabulary_would_regress, consumed by skill-base.sh's skill_postflight_update) only blocks a regression between two RANKED statuses (not_started..completed, 8 of 13 enum values). partial/blocked/abandoned/expanded/hold are deliberately unranked, so a write FROM a ranked status (e.g. completed) TO an unranked one (e.g. partial) is never blocked by this clamp, even when status_clamp_mode=monotonic-max is explicitly passed. The clamp is also opt-in (empty by default; only 'monotonic-max' when force_invoked=true), so an ordinary postflight call never consults it at all. update-task-status.sh itself has no terminal-state guard on postflight writes (only skill_preflight_update guards terminal states, and only for preflight calls).
